web_evidence.note: The University of New Brunswick dissertation's Desperation analysis identifies an interior diegesis as delivered by the third-person narrator and treats characters' first-person interior reactions as voices framed within that narration.

web_evidence.title: Stephen King Writing Styles in Desperation

web_evidence.title: Narrative Embedding in the Postmodern American Novel with Reference to Stephen King's Desperation
web_evidence.note: This scholarly structural study distinguishes the novel's framing discourse from subordinated character-told chronicles and other embedded narratives, helping prevent local first-person material from being mistaken for an alternating base person.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person: multiple quotes externally narrate characters while moving into David's or Johnny's consciousness, and the whole-book POV description agrees. The 'you' in q00104 is a generic free-indirect maxim within third-person narration, while other first- and second-person forms are dialogue. Scholarly structural sources show that character-told histories and interior first-person voices are embedded within the frame, not autonomous base sections, so they do not justify ALTERNATING. No accessible authorized sustained excerpt was found, but the concordance of diagnostic quotations, a scholarly narratological analysis, and an explicit whole-book account leaves no substantive person conflict.
